arabic text: AKBER MERE JAWAN, KISKO BULAYE MAA... ZAINAB KI\nLO KHABAR, ABID HAI NATAWAN...
english translation text: Akbar, my young son—whom should your mother call now?\nGo and care for Zainab; Abid is weak and helpless.

arabic text:
DASHTE BALA KO CHAUR KAR, KHAKE SHIFA KO
AURDH KAR
AY FAKHRE KIBRIYA SUNO, KEHTI HU HAATH JAUR KAR
KAYSE CHALEGI MAA, AE MERE NAWJAWA
english translation text:
Leaving the plain of calamity and
covering herself in Karbala’s dust,
O pride of the Almighty, listen as I fold my hands in plea:
How will your mother continue, O my young son?

arabic text:
KISMAT KI PAAS BAA HAI WO, KHAYRUN NISA KI
JAAN HAI WO
GHURBAT KI INTIHAN HUWI, GHAYRO KE DARMIYA HAI
WO
SHEHZADI YE JINA, SEHTI HAI ZAKHMIYA
english translation text:
She is the protector of destiny,
the life of Khayrun Nisa.
Her homelessness has reached its limit;
she stands among strangers.
This princess endures wounds upon wounds.

arabic text:
QATIL KI RAH MERE PISAR, SAJJAD KA HAI HAM
SAFAR
KAMTO NAHI HAI YEH SITAM, SEHTA RAHA HAI RO
MAGAR
KAYSE SAHE BHALA, BIMAR KARWAN
english translation text:
Your killer walks beside my son,
while Sajjad is his fellow traveller.
This cruelty is not small;
he endures it while weeping.
How can the sick leader bear the caravan’s burden?

arabic text:
MAINE SUNI HAI YE SADA, KEHTE HAI SHAAM MAI
SABHI
BADLA ALI KA LENGE HAM, BINTE ALI SE AAJ HI
PATHAR SE HAI BHARI, LOGO KE JOLIYA
english translation text:
I have heard everyone in Shaam saying:
Today we will take revenge
for Ali upon Ali’s daughter.
The people’s laps are filled with stones.

arabic text: PALA HAI JISNE UMR BHAR, AKBER TUJHE HIJAB ME\nGHAZI KE SAAMNE BHI WO, BETA RAHI NIQAAB MEI\nGHAYRO ME BERIDA, JAATI HAI ALLAMA
english translation text: Akbar, she who raised you all your life behind the veil,\nwho remained veiled even before Ghazi,\nnow goes unveiled among strangers—your learned aunt.

arabic text:
NOKE SINA KO DEKH KAR, YAWAR YE KEHRAHI THI
MAA
AA DIKH TU HI NAWJAWAN, MADAR KA APNI IMTAHAN
AANKHE NA BAND KAR, GHAYRAT YE ASMAA
english translation text:
Seeing the point of the spear,
the mother cried out, O Yawar:
Come, young son—witness your mother’s trial.
Do not close your eyes; even the heavens are ashamed.
